fixture_and_assertion_contract.initial_inventory_and_xp: Vanilla give commands add seven diamonds and five bread; experience commands add 23 levels and 17 points. Native synced state is observed before snapshot and entry.
fixture_and_assertion_contract.crew_room: After the first verified return, a supported dry room, Boombox, crafting table and Charter are placed in the disposable save. Founding, facility registration and mission dispatch use normal client actions.
fixture_and_assertion_contract.arena_arrival: After selecting an actual route, the explicitly logged fixture loads nearby chunks and teleports to that selected destination. The production builder, arrival and cache code create the visible arena state; the fixture does not add elapsed time, defeats, rewards or a room clear.
fixture_and_assertion_contract.cache_scout: Six live cache previews with actual reward labels, colors, positions and distances; zero completed rooms is asserted. Preview capture does not demonstrate a claim.

artifacts.download_blocker: The authenticated browser security boundary blocked archive download; API metadata is preserved without treating it as downloaded or independently hash-verified bytes.
artifacts.digest_scope: Each digest below is GitHub-reported SHA-256 of an artifact ZIP, not the SHA-256 of its enclosed mod JAR.
artifacts.provisional_local_jar_exclusion: The provisional local JAR omitted generated assets and is not used as release or checksum evidence.

fixture_limits: Cache and six-room route GameTests run production builders and reward code with injected recordDefeat counters and advanced test clocks. They do not establish naturally played room clears or continuous traversal.

Synergy runtime tests separately use actual director-created session-owned actors and production primary/secondary damage handling, including real virtual defeats, obstruction, owner rejection and native-state preservation. Controlled actor placement and short clocks are not full-session pacing evidence.

Style Library settlement tests supply qualifying event data to production transactions and use a persisted mission deadline. They do not play complete Tag/Hill/Showdown rounds or wait real mission minutes; codec/handler tests are not remote socket tests.

The client arena arrival is a documented disposable-world teleport/chunk-load fixture. Fifteen required captures do not prove human connector traversal, a cache claim, a completed arena or a completed six-room circuit.
The visual audit does not fabricate learned styles, reward history or a populated artifact build. A fresh locked library, empty history or running mission retains that meaning.

CI capture pixels remain undownloaded and unreviewed. The separate exact-source local replay has 15 unchanged, hash-checked and directly reviewed native captures. Its original on-disk log is incomplete; a clearly labeled tool-stdout excerpt preserves the observed completion. No CI artifact byte equality is established.
Pinned provider jobs cover the identified representative mobs, dimensions and one Firebolt adapter, not every creature, boss, spell, summon, recipe, capability, mod version or combined modpack.
Normal saved shutdown is covered; forced crashes, disk failures and arbitrary third-party capability recovery are not certified.
Machine checks do not establish human thirty-minute pacing, economy balance, prolonged Endless performance or multiplayer scale.

Dungeons I/II inform original bounded run mechanics; neither full native equipment catalogue nor proprietary assets are imported. Custom arenas are bounded data-pack layouts, not arbitrary NBT imports or an in-game editor.

An initial independent local GameTest setup failed before generated catalogues were present; this created the disposable audit world. Authored asset generation and the corrected local build then passed, followed by the native client replay. No all-44 local retest is claimed; the final nine-configuration 44-test result is the separately identified CI evidence.
